findings.claim: Every failure path in the one-run runner discards the causal error without binding it, logging it, or reporting an incident, so a halted paid shadow leaves only a generic code (`PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_PRE_DISPATCH_FAILED` / `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` / `TERMINAL_WRITE_UNKNOWN`) and no record of why, in a system that forbids retrying to find out.
findings.reproduction: `rg -n 'console\.|reportOperationalIncident' lib/promptRefinerShadowRunner.ts` returns nothing, and both catch clauses bind no error variable. The route cannot compensate: app/api/admin/prompt-refiner/shadow-run/execute/route.ts:152-153 returns `promptRefinerShadowRunnerErrorResponse(error)` before ever reaching its `console.error` at line 160. Concretely, tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs `failAfterIntentAt` throws `new Error("after intent")` and the only observable output is the 503 code — the message reaches no sink. lib/maintenance.ts:26 shows the project's existing `reportOperationalIncident` channel for exactly this class of event.

findings.claim: When `recordPromptRefinerShadowDispatchIntent` returns `reservation_expired` it has already transitioned the row to `expired`, so the runner's subsequent release necessarily fails and the operator is told `PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_PRE_DISPATCH_RELEASE_FAILED` ("could not close its reservation") about a reservation that is in fact correctly closed.
findings.reproduction: lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:782-786 sets `status: "expired"` and returns `{ok:false, reason:"reservation_expired"}`; that `!intent.ok` branch (runner line 205-211) throws inside `onDispatch`, so the runner's catch at line 215 sees `attemptId === null` and calls `dependencies.release(reservation)`. lib/promptRefinerReservationAuthority.ts:316 refuses any non-`reserved` row with `reservation_not_active`, so `released.ok` is false and the runner refuses with the release-failure code instead of the real `reservation_expired` cause. No test covers this path: tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs has no fixture where `recordIntent` returns `ok:false`.

findings.claim: The budget guard compares against the literal `300_000` rather than the route's declared `maxDuration`, so lowering `export const maxDuration` would leave a 240 s admission budget that exceeds the platform cap with no gate failing.
findings.reproduction: Change `export const maxDuration = 300;` to `60` in app/api/admin/prompt-refiner/shadow-run/execute/route.ts and run `npm run test:prompt-refiner-shadow-live-adapter`; it stays green, and `promptRefinerShadowRunContractProblems()` still returns `[]`. tests/cronClientTimeouts.test.mjs:52 shows the project's existing idiom for parsing `export const maxDuration` out of a route and binding it to an in-code budget.

verdict.nextAction: All three round-1 findings are addressed (rate limit moved after strict-body validation and raised to 2/min·8/day, the sweep fixture now matches `sweepPromptRefinerShadowUnknowns`'s real shape, and the `INTENT_MISSING` path releases its reservation once); merge as-is and optionally fold the three recorded items into a follow-up.
